questions.message: Explain the promo in plain words.
questions.shown:
Answer to the contractor:
The promo is a deferred-interest offer. Interest builds up from the start but isn't charged if the full amount financed, $30,000.00, is paid off within the promo period of 12 months. If any balance remains when that period ends, all the built-up interest is added to the balance, which the screen shows as $4,409.69. Regular monthly payments of $440.40 are due throughout, and that is over her $300.00 budget by $140.40.

Line the contractor reads aloud to the homeowner:
With the promo, interest builds up from the start, but it isn't charged if the full $30,000.00 is paid off within 12 months. If any balance is left after that, all the built-up interest is added, with a cliff of $4,409.69. The payment is $440.40 a month at 15.99% APR over 15 years.

questions.message: What happens if she doesn't pay off the promo in time?
questions.shown:
Answer to the contractor:
Under the Promo's deferred-interest terms, interest builds up from the start. If any balance remains when the promo period ends, all of the built-up interest is added to the balance. The figure on screen for that is $4,409.69, and regular monthly payments of $440.40 are due throughout. Paying off $30,000.00 within 12 months avoids that interest being charged.

Line the contractor reads aloud to the homeowner:
With the Promo, interest builds up from the start, and if any balance is left when the 12 months end, all of that built-up interest gets added to the balance, which is $4,409.69 on screen. The Promo's payment is $440.40 a month at 15.99% APR over 15 years.

grounding.problem: The read-aloud line says the built-up interest 'gets added to the balance, which is $4,409.69 on screen.' The most natural reading is that the balance is $4,409.69. In the facts, $4,409.69 is the deferred interest added if the promo isn't paid off in time (the cliff). The balance to pay off within the 12 promo months is $30,000.00. So the homeowner hears the figure attached to the wrong item. The answer to the contractor is fine; only the read-aloud line has this problem.
